title: No Sitting State Comptroller as Knesset Defies Court-Ordered Revote; Government Escalates to First-Ever High Court Defiance
detail: On July 5, 2026, with Michael Rabello's term as state comptroller due to begin, Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana confirmed to the High Court of Justice that he would not hold the revote the Court had ordered on July 2 over the secret-ballot violation in Rabello's election — declaring 'the Knesset has already spoken.' Ohana had first rejected the Court's advisory recommendation to redo the vote on June 21. Because Rabello's original mandate was voided and no revote was held, and outgoing comptroller Matanyahu Englman's term was not extended, Israel has had no sitting state comptroller since that Sunday — leaving the office legally mandated to audit government conduct, including the October 7 failures, vacant. The same week, Netanyahu's Cabinet voted unanimously to explicitly defy a separate High Court ruling requiring the national broadcast media regulator to keep functioning — the first time in Israeli history a government has declared outright it will not abide by a Supreme Court ruling. Former PM Naftali Bennett warned 'this leads to anarchy,' and all of Israel's living former Supreme Court chief justices issued a joint statement calling court defiance 'the final nail in the coffin of democracy.'

media.caption: Netanyahu's Cabinet votes to defy a High Court ruling for the first time in Israeli history, deepening the institutional crisis around October 7 accountability
